rows.selection_reason: With no completed experiments, the primary uncertainty is the baseline performance of the simplest RNA-only setup, which anchors all subsequent comparisons. config_001 (rna_only, singleprofile, pca_n2000) is the most minimal configuration: it uses PCA (a standard, fast, well-understood encoder) with a single profile, introducing no learned encoders, no aggregation, and no fusion. This establishes (1) the floor performance for the RNA modality, (2) a reference for the singleprofile setting, and (3) a known value for PCA_n2000, which is the RNA encoder shared by configs 016–027 in the multimodal space. By starting here, every later experiment—whether adding a better RNA encoder, switching to multiprofile, or introducing an image modality—can be interpreted as a controlled increment over a clear, simple baseline. Under a limited budget, this single experiment maximally reduces uncertainty about the fundamental signal available in the data before committing to more complex (and costlier) configurations.

Evidence: We have only one completed experiment (config_001: rna_only, singleprofile, pca_n2000 → acc 0.485, F1 0.464), which gives a weak RNA-only baseline and tells us nothing about whether the image modality carries useful signal. This is a multimodal cellular profiling study, so the single most consequential design question is whether the image branch contributes any predictive value at all. Question tested: config_010 (image_only, singleprofile, resnet50) provides a clean unimodal image baseline using a standard, well-established backbone, directly comparable in structure to config_001. Why it is the best next experiment: (1) If image accuracy is substantially higher than 0.485, it validates the multimodal direction and justifies investing subsequent experiments in fusion strategies; if it is similarly low, it suggests the image modality may not be informative and we should focus budget on RNA encoder and profile improvements. (2) It partitions the remaining 50 untested configs into two strategic branches (image-useful vs. image-not-useful), dramatically reducing search-space uncertainty with a single run. (3) resnet50 is a reasonable, fast-to-train first probe before committing to the heavier ViT-L variants. No other single experiment reduces as much uncertainty about the overall architecture under the limited budget.

Evidence: config_001 (RNA-only, singleprofile, pca_n2000) achieves 48.5% accuracy, while config_010 (image-only, singleprofile, resnet50) achieves only 20.8%, establishing RNA as the dominant modality with a large gap. The key uncertainty now is whether the profile setting (single vs. multi) and aggregation strategy can improve RNA performance, which is the foundational design choice for all subsequent multimodal experiments. This experiment (config_002: RNA-only, multiprofile, pca_n2000, avgpool) directly tests whether aggregating multiple cell profiles via average pooling improves over the single-profile baseline, while holding the encoder constant. It is the minimal, cleanest extension of config_001, isolating the multiprofile+aggregation variable. If it helps, it validates the multiprofile direction and informs all multimodal configs; if it does not, it prunes a large portion of the search space (all multiprofile variants) under a limited budget. Choosing avgpool over transformer first is conservative: it tests whether any aggregation benefit exists before committing to a more complex aggregator.

Evidence: config_002 (RNA, multi-profile, PCA, avgpool) achieved 0.591 acc, a substantial +10.6% gain over config_001 (single-profile, 0.485), confirming that multi-profile aggregation is a high-impact design choice. However, we only have one data point on aggregation method (avgpool). Uncertainty: It is unclear whether a more expressive aggregation (transformer) further improves over simple averaging, which would change the aggregation choice for all downstream multimodal experiments. This experiment (config_003) isolates exactly one variable—aggregation method (transformer vs avgpool)—while holding RNA encoder (PCA n2000), profile setting (multi), and modality (RNA-only) constant, making it a clean A/B comparison with config_002. If transformer significantly outperforms avgpool, it signals that learned aggregation is worth pursuing across encoders and modalities; if it is comparable, avgpool is sufficient and budget is better spent exploring encoder choice or multimodal fusion. Under a limited budget, resolving this binary design question with a controlled comparison is more informative than jumping to a less certain multimodal or new-encoder configuration.

Evidence: RNA-only with multiprofile+avgpool (config_002, acc=0.591) is the clear best so far, while image-only is very weak (config_010, acc=0.208). We also know avgpool > transformer for aggregation. The critical open question is whether the image modality provides any complementary signal when combined with the strong RNA features, which is the central premise of this multimodal study. Config_018 (multimodal, multiprofile, pca_n2000, resnet50, avgpool, concat) is the most direct logical extension of our best result: it keeps the proven RNA setup (multiprofile + avgpool + pca_n2000) and adds the image branch with the simplest standard fusion (concat). If it beats 0.591, multimodal fusion is validated and we can explore weighted fusion and better image encoders; if it does not, we learn that image adds no value and can redirect budget toward RNA encoder improvements (scvi/scgpt). This single experiment resolves the highest-uncertainty design decision under the limited budget.

Evidence: Our best result (config_018, acc=0.619) uses pca_n2000 as the RNA encoder in a multimodal, multiprofile, avgpool, concat setup. All completed experiments have used only PCA as the RNA encoder, leaving the learned-encoder dimension (scvi_n200, scgpt) completely unexplored. Question: config_030 is a clean single-variable change from config_018, swapping pca_n2000 → scvi_n200 while holding multimodal, multiprofile, resnet50, avgpool, and concat fixed. This directly tests whether a nonlinear, biologically-informed learned encoder outperforms linear PCA in the multimodal fusion context. Why this is the best next experiment: The RNA encoder is a fundamental architectural choice with potentially large upside—if scvi captures richer cell-type structure than PCA, the gain would transfer to all downstream multimodal configurations. Conversely, if it does not improve over PCA, we can confidently rule out learned encoders and concentrate remaining budget on image-encoder and fusion-strategy variations. Compared to testing weighted fusion (config_019), which is a more incremental change with likely smaller effect size, the encoder choice carries higher information value per experiment under a limited budget.

Evidence: The current best configuration (config_030: multimodal, multiprofile, scvi_n200, resnet50, avgpool, concat) achieves acc=0.632/F1=0.607, and all multimodal results so far use concat fusion. The fusion strategy is a critical, completely untested design axis in the multimodal setting where two modalities of potentially different informativeness (RNA >> image) are combined. Question: Does weighted fusion outperform simple concatenation when combining a strong RNA signal with a weaker image signal? config_031 changes only the fusion method (concat → weighted) relative to config_030, providing a clean single-variable comparison. Why this is the best next experiment: It directly exploits the current best configuration while resolving the single largest untested design decision in the multimodal pipeline. If weighted fusion helps, it indicates the modalities contribute unequally and a learned or fixed weighting is beneficial; if it does not, we confirm concat is sufficient and can redirect budget toward other axes (e.g., image encoder choice or scgpt). This is the highest-information-per-experiment choice under the limited budget.

The current best is config_031 (scvi_n200, resnet50, avgpool, weighted; acc=0.678). The largest single improvement came from switching concat→weighted fusion (+4.6%), and SCVI gave a modest boost over PCA. The one major untested axis in the current best is the image encoder: we have only used resnet50, which alone scored a very weak 0.208. Config_037 changes only the image encoder to imagenet_vit_l (a substantially larger, pretrained ViT), keeping the otherwise-best settings (scvi_n200, multiprofile, avgpool, weighted). This directly tests whether a stronger image encoder can extract more informative morphological features that complement the RNA signal under weighted fusion. If it improves, it justifies further investment in the image branch; if it does not, it confirms the image modality's marginal contribution is encoder-limited and we should focus remaining budget on RNA-side or fusion refinements. This is a clean single-variable extension of the current best, making it the highest-information next experiment under a tight budget.

The current best configuration (config_037: scvi_n200 + imagenet_vit_l + avgpool + weighted, acc=0.706) establishes that multimodal with multiprofile, avgpool aggregation, weighted fusion, and a strong image encoder is the dominant design. The remaining untested variable in this top region is the RNA encoder: we've seen pca_n2000 → scvi_n200 yield a modest gain (~1.3%), but scgpt has never been tested. Config_049 (scgpt, imagenet_vit_l, avgpool, weighted) directly swaps only the RNA encoder in the best-known setup, giving a clean comparison against config_037. This is the highest-value experiment because it (1) exploits the strongest known configuration, (2) tests whether the RNA encoder is still a performance bottleneck or whether scvi_n200 is near-saturated, and (3) if scgpt outperforms, it opens a new optimization axis; if not, it confirms scvi_n200 is sufficient and redirects budget toward other untested dimensions (e.g., transformer aggregation with vit_l). Under a limited budget, this single experiment resolves the most consequential remaining uncertainty about the top-performing region.

The current best config (config_037: scvi_n200, vit_l, multiprofile, avgpool, weighted) achieves 0.706 acc. The strongest evidence from RNA-only experiments shows avgpool (0.591) substantially outperforms transformer (0.519) aggregation, but this has not been confirmed in the multimodal regime with the top-performing encoders. Config_039 changes only the aggregation from avgpool to transformer while holding all other variables at their best-known values (scvi_n200, vit_l, multiprofile, weighted). This single-variable test will clarify whether the avgpool advantage persists with a stronger image encoder and weighted fusion, or whether transformer aggregation becomes competitive in the multimodal setting. If transformer underperforms (as expected), it confirms avgpool as the correct choice and directs remaining budget toward other unexplored axes. If transformer is competitive or better, it opens a new optimization direction. This is the highest-information experiment because it resolves a key architectural uncertainty at the top of the performance landscape with a clean, interpretable comparison.
